title: Mean change under a sign restriction
statement: Let $n,k$ be nonnegative integers, let $f:\\{-1,1\\}^n\\to\\mathbb R$ be Fourier-regular at level $k$ with bound $\\varepsilon\\ge0$, let $J\\subseteq\\{1,\\ldots,n\\}$, and fix signs on the coordinates outside $J$. If the number of coordinates outside $J$ is at most $k$, then the absolute difference between the mean of the resulting restriction of $f$ (averaged over the free coordinates in $J$) and the mean of $f$ on the full cube is at most $2^k\\varepsilon$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is Fourier-regular at level $k$ with bound $\\varepsilon$
$J$ is a subset of the $n$ coordinates
A sign assignment is fixed on coordinates outside $J$
The number of coordinates outside $J$ is at most $k$
